schema_review.rationale: The shared s1300 -> s1400 -> s1401 chain registers the complete installed 1.3.0 no-vector Server database on SQLite, seekDB and OceanBase. SQLite and OceanBase may enable Code because its local cache is separate from this database; exact installed source inventories match the existing no-vector baselines. Admission preserves that ownership boundary instead of rejecting the flag. The installed-release matrix includes both Code-enabled backends and requires the source-built index to retain its fingerprint, symbols and immutable cache files through target Server queries. Vector profiles and embedded seekDB Code storage still require their own registered transitions. Frozen migration schemas, domain resources and released revision checksums remain unchanged. The chain preserves historical bytes, Source references, Candidate history and pending intents, fences old workers, and validates projections, Dream tasks, Processing ownership and live readiness. Registered maintenance shares the target lock, backup providers and durable recovery evidence; managed startup and identity admission do not perform schema changes. Processing mode changes and Atomic current projection repairs preserve revision and immutable authority, and resume from the original recovery point. Publication requires complete installed-release acceptance, repeated apply, old-startup rejection, background Worker execution and fresh-schema equivalence. Optional profile and complete native failure recovery acceptance remain incomplete.
